newsitem.title: UK: UK may take tough line on Bass deal.
newsitem.headline: UK may take tough line on Bass deal.

text.p: Britain's trade and industry secretary Margaret Beckett looks likely to demand major concessions from British brewer Bass if its planned tie up with Carlsberg-Tetley is to go ahead, brewing analysts said on Thursday.

They said a delay in publishing the report suggested the new Labour government would not block the deal, but wanted to impose conditions on the merger, which would give Bass more than 35 percent of the UK beer market.
"It's probably the accepted view that if they wanted to stop the deal completely it would be in the open by now," said one brewing analyst who asked not to be identified.

He said the key question was whether stringent conditions might deter Bass from proceeding with the deal. If the brewer were asked to sell large portions of its pub estate this would go a long way to removing the cost saving benefits of the deal with Carlsberg, the analyst said.
Analysts said they believed a decision ought to come out in the next week, but stressed that this was pure guesswork.

If the deal was blocked or conditions imposed which were unsatisfactory to Bass, the company can sell its 50 percent stake in Carlsberg-Tetley to Allied Domecq Plc for 110 million pounds ($183.3 million) and claim a 30 million pound refund from Allied. Bass bought the 50 percent stake from Allied last August for 200 million stg.

Carlsberg, the Danish brewer that held the rest, agreed to contribute its interest to Bass, together with 20 million pounds, in exchange for 20 percent of the merged Bass Brewers/Carlsberg-Tetley business.
Bass said it could not comment on speculation that Beckett would take a tough line on the merger.

The Department of Trade and Industry had no comment on the timing of publication of the Monopolies and Mergers Commission report on the deal, which was originally agreed 10 months ago. The MMC report was sent to the DTI on March 24. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717 ($ = 0.600 British Pounds)
